section: Chapter Three — Idols and Their Accessories
subtitle: When idols and their appurtenances become forbidden; Rambam on astrological-talismanic magic
author: Moses Maimonides
intro: Rambam's commentary on Tractate Avodah Zarah — the laws of idolatry, forbidden commercial dealings, libation wine, and the nullification of idols. Original 12th-century Judeo-Arabic with English translation.

aligned.ja: משנה [א]
aligned.en: Mishnah [1]

aligned.ja: יזעמון אהל הד'א אלשאן אנה אד'א חלת אלשמס בדרג'ה מן דרג' אלפלך אי דרג'ה כאנת, יעמל טלסם לתלך אלדרג'ה עלי מת'ל אלצורה אלתי תנסב לתלך אלדרג'ה, פתט'הר לה קוי פי אלוג'וד פי מעאני תלך אלצורה ואלאפעאל אלתי תנסב להא.
aligned.en: The practitioners of this art[^1] hold that when the sun enters a given degree of the celestial sphere — whichever degree that may be — one should fashion a talisman (*ṭilasm*)[^2] for that degree in the form ascribed to it, whereupon the powers belonging to that image and to the actions attributed to it will manifest in the world.

pairs.en: The practitioners of this art[^1]

pairs.ja: אד'א חלת אלשמס בדרג'ה מן דרג' אלפלך
pairs.en: when the sun enters a given degree of the celestial sphere
one should fashion a talisman (*ṭilasm*)[^2] for that degree
in the form ascribed to it
the powers belonging to that image will manifest in the world

fn.1: "The practitioners of this art" — lit. *ahl hādhā al-shaʾn*, "the people of this matter/discipline," referring to the practitioners of Hellenistic-Neoplatonic talismanic astrology, who believed that fashioning a physical image corresponding to a planet or zodiac degree at the precise moment of the sun's transit could channel that celestial power.
fn.2: *Ṭilasm* (pl. *ṭalāsim*) — the Arabic term for a talisman or magical seal, derived from Greek *telesma*. Rambam uses the word technically throughout this passage to denote images constructed to draw down planetary or stellar power. The entire passage reflects his firsthand knowledge of the Hermetic-Neoplatonic tradition of *ʿilm al-ṭalāsim* (the science of talismans), well attested in tenth-century Arabic encyclopedic literature.

aligned.ja: פהם יבכ'רון לד'לך אלטלסם וידעון לה ויעט'מונה מתי מא חלת אלשמס בתלך אלדרג'ה, והד'א נוע מן ג'מלה אנואע אלטלאסם.
aligned.en: They accordingly perfume that talisman, invoke it, and venerate it whenever the sun re-enters that degree. This is one species among the various species of talismanic practice.

pairs.en: perfume that talisman
invoke it, and venerate it

pairs.ja: מתי מא חלת אלשמס בתלך אלדרג'ה
pairs.en: whenever the sun re-enters that degree
one species among the various species of talismanic practice

aligned.ja: פפי מוצ'ע ר' מאיר כאן ענדהם הד'א אלנוע מן אלטלאסם וקד עלמת אן ר' מאיר חייש למיעוט פלד'לך ג'על ג'מיע אלצור אסורין לכון בעצ'הא יעמל לאלעבאדה מרה פי אלעאם ענד חלול אלשמס בתלך אלדרג'ה.
aligned.en: In the locale of R. Meir this particular type of talisman was current, and R. Meir was mindful of the minority[^3] — that is, he feared that even an image held in a small number of hands might at some point be fashioned for actual worship, once a year, when the sun entered the relevant degree. He therefore ruled that all [human] images are forbidden.

pairs.en: R. Meir was mindful of the minority[^3]
ruled that all [human] images are forbidden
fashioned for actual worship, once a year
when the sun entered the relevant degree

fn.3: "Mindful of the minority" (*ḥayyish le-miʿuṭ*) — a halakhic principle: one rules stringently to account for the minority of cases in which an otherwise neutral object might be used for a prohibited purpose.

aligned.ja: וחכמים לא חישי למיעוט ויקולון אנה קד תעמל לאלזינה פקט. פאד'א כאן פי יד אלצורה שי ממא ד'כר תנא קמא או מא זאדוא פי אלבריתא והי סיף ועטרה וטבעת פחיניד' נעלם צחיח אנה עמל ברצד ובכ'ור ודעוי ותקריב כמא הו משהור ענד אהל הד'א אלשאן, ובשרט אן תכון הד'ה אלצור על פתח מדינה.
aligned.en: The Sages, however, are not mindful of the minority; they hold that such an image is ordinarily made for decorative purposes only. Therefore, if the image held in someone's hand bears one of the attributes enumerated by the first Tanna[^4] — or the additional items listed in the *Baraita*, namely a sword, a crown, and a ring — we know with certainty that it was made with astronomical observation, fumigation, invocation, and offering, as is well known among those versed in this discipline, provided that these images stand at the entrance to a city.

pairs.en: The Sages are not mindful of the minority
made for decorative purposes only
the first Tanna[^4]
made with astronomical observation, fumigation, invocation, and offering

pairs.ja: ובשרט אן תכון הד'ה אלצור על פתח מדינה
pairs.en: provided that these images stand at the entrance to a city

fn.4: "The first Tanna" (*Tanna qamma*) — the anonymous first opinion cited in the Mishnah, typically representing the majority or normative position.

aligned.ja: ולא כ'לאף בינהם אן ג'מיע אלצור אלד'י פי אלקרי ואלמגאשר אסורין לאנהא באלחקיקה אנמא עמלת הנאך לתעבד, לאן ליס תלך אלמואצ'ע מואצ'ע זינה פנקול לאלזינה עמלת, ולו לם יכון פי ידה שי. והלכה כחכמים.
aligned.en: There is no dispute, however, that all images found in villages and rural settlements are forbidden, for in truth they were made there solely for worship: those localities are not places of ornament, so that one could say they were made for decoration, even if the image holds nothing in its hand. The law follows the Sages.

pairs.ja: ג'מיע אלצור אלד'י פי אלקרי ואלמגאשר אסורין
pairs.en: all images found in villages and rural settlements are forbidden
they were made there solely for worship
those localities are not places of ornament
The law follows the Sages

aligned.ja: משנה [ב]
aligned.en: Mishnah [2]

aligned.ja: תבנית יד ורגל, ליס אנה יד צנם אנכסר לאן הד'ה הי שברי צלמים, ואנמא מן אול עמלה עמל צורהֵ יד פקט או צורהֵ רג'ל, וכד'לך צורהֵ אי עצ'ו עמל.
aligned.en: "The form of a hand or foot" — this does not mean the hand of a broken idol, for that would fall under the rubric of "fragments of idols."[^5] Rather, it means that from the outset, when it was fashioned, it was made as the image of a hand alone, or the image of a foot alone, or the image of any other limb in isolation.

pairs.en: The form of a hand or foot
this does not mean the hand of a broken idol
that would fall under the rubric of "fragments of idols."[^5]

pairs.ja: מן אול עמלה עמל צורהֵ יד פקט
pairs.en: from the outset it was made as the image of a hand alone

fn.5: "Fragments of idols" (*shivrei ṣelamim*) — broken pieces of an idol that has lost its complete form; these are subject to a different legal analysis than independently crafted partial images.

aligned.ja: ומן צנעתה יתבין הל הו מן אול עמלה עמל מפרד או אנכסר מן צורה כאמלה.
aligned.en: From the manner of its crafting one can tell whether it was made from the outset as an independent piece or whether it broke off from a complete figure.

pairs.en: From the manner of its crafting one can tell
made from the outset as an independent piece
broke off from a complete figure

aligned.ja: משנה [ג]
aligned.en: Mishnah [3]

aligned.ja: צורת חמה ולבנה, ליס מענאה אן יג'ד דאירה פיקול הד'ה אלשמס, או קוס מן דאירה פיקול הד'ה אלקמר, ואנמא אהל אלטלאסם ינסבון אלי אלכואכב צור, חתי יקולון צורהֵ זחל צורהֵ שיך' אסוד והרם, וצורהֵ אלזהרה צורהֵ ג'אריה חסנה מחליה ד'הב, וצורהֵ אלשמס צורה מלך מתוג' מסתקר פי עג'לה.
aligned.en: "The form of the sun and the form of the moon" — this does not mean that one finds a disc and says, "this is the sun," or finds an arc of a disc and says, "this is the moon." Rather, the practitioners of talismanic lore attribute specific bodily forms to the planets, so that they say: the form of Saturn is an aged black man,[^6] stooped; the form of Venus is a beautiful young woman adorned with gold jewelry; the form of the sun is a crowned king seated securely in a chariot.[^7]

pairs.ja: ליס מענאה אן יג'ד דאירה פיקול הד'ה אלשמס
pairs.en: this does not mean that one finds a disc and says, "this is the sun"

pairs.ja: אהל אלטלאסם ינסבון אלי אלכואכב צור
pairs.en: the practitioners of talismanic lore attribute specific bodily forms to the planets

pairs.ja: צורהֵ זחל צורהֵ שיך' אסוד והרם
pairs.en: the form of Saturn is an aged black man,[^6] stooped

pairs.ja: צורהֵ אלזהרה צורהֵ ג'אריה חסנה מחליה ד'הב
pairs.en: the form of Venus is a beautiful young woman adorned with gold jewelry

pairs.ja: צורהֵ אלשמס צורה מלך מתוג' מסתקר פי עג'לה
pairs.en: the form of the sun is a crowned king seated securely in a chariot.[^7]

fn.6: Rambam's description of Saturn's talismanic form as "an aged black man, stooped" reflects the standard Hermetic-Arabic iconography of Zuḥal (Saturn) found in works such as *Ghāyat al-Ḥakīm* (the *Picatrix*) and related astrological-magical texts.
fn.7: The description of the sun's form as a crowned king in a chariot is likewise a stock image in the Hermetic-Neoplatonic astral-magic tradition. Rambam presents these as baseless fictions fabricated by practitioners but explains that the Torah's prohibition targets precisely these culturally recognized forms.

aligned.ja: והכד'א ינסבון לג'מיע אלברוג' ואלדרארי צור כת'ירה, והם פי תלך אלצור מכ'תלפין אכ'תלאפא כת'ירא, לאנהא אקאויל כאד'בה, ואלכד'ב עלי שי מא יכת'ר ויתסע בלא שך. פקולה צורת חמה ולבנה יריד בה אן יג'ד אלצורה אלמנסובה לאלשמס ואלצורה אלמנסובה לאלקמר עלי אי מד'הב כאן.
aligned.en: In this fashion they assign many forms to all the constellations of the zodiac[^8] and to the planets (*al-darārī*).[^9] Among these forms they differ greatly from one another, because these accounts are fabricated, and falsehood in any matter multiplies and expands without bound. When the Mishnah says "the form of the sun and the form of the moon" it means whatever form is attributed to the sun and whatever form is attributed to the moon, on whichever school's account.

pairs.ja: ינסבון לג'מיע אלברוג' ואלדרארי צור כת'ירה
pairs.en: they assign many forms to all the constellations of the zodiac[^8] and to the planets (*al-darārī*)[^9]
they differ greatly from one another
these accounts are fabricated

pairs.ja: אלכד'ב עלי שי מא יכת'ר ויתסע בלא שך
pairs.en: falsehood in any matter multiplies and expands without bound
on whichever school's account

fn.8: "Constellations of the zodiac" (*al-burūj*) — the twelve signs of the zodiac (Aries through Pisces), each associated in astrological tradition with its own set of talismanic images, decans, and degrees.
fn.9: *Al-darārī* — the Arabic term for the seven classical planets (sun, moon, Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Venus, Mercury), so called because of their continuous motion through the fixed stars.

aligned.ja: והדרקון, צורהֵ שכ'ץ לה אג'נחה ופלוס כת'ירה פי ט'הרה בין אג'נחתה כפלוס אלסמך, והד'ה אלצורה כאנת איצ'א מעט'מה ענדהם לאנהם כאנוא ינסבונהא לג'ז מן אג'זא אלפלך.
aligned.en: As for the dragon (*ha-dereqon*): its form is that of a figure with wings and many scales along its back between its wings, like the scales of a fish. This figure, too, was venerated by them, for they attributed it to a portion of the celestial sphere.

pairs.en: As for the dragon (*ha-dereqon*)

pairs.ja: צורהֵ שכ'ץ לה אג'נחה ופלוס כת'ירה
pairs.en: its form is that of a figure with wings and many scales
like the scales of a fish
venerated by them
they attributed it to a portion of the celestial sphere

aligned.ja: ואכ'ברני רג'ל ממן ישאר אליה פי הד'א אלפן אן הד'ה אלצורה הי לג'וזהר אלקמר, ואנהא תפעל עלי צפהֵ כד'א פי וקת כד'א פתות'ר אלכד'א ואלכד'א, וסאלתה ען אלכתאב אלד'י ד'כר פיה ד'לך אני לם תמר בי קט הד'ה אלצורה, פזעם אנה קלדה מעלמה ושיכ'ה הד'ה אלצורה מע ג'מלהֵ מא אסר אליה.
aligned.en: A man who is regarded as an authority in this discipline told me that this figure belongs to the lunar node (*al-jawzahar*)[^10] and that it acts in such-and-such a manner at such-and-such a time, producing such-and-such effects. I asked him for the book in which this was written — for I had never come across this figure before — and he claimed that he had received it by chain of tradition from his teacher and from his teacher's teacher, along with everything else he had pointed to.

pairs.ja: אכ'ברני רג'ל ממן ישאר אליה פי הד'א אלפן
pairs.en: A man who is regarded as an authority in this discipline told me
this figure belongs to the lunar node (*al-jawzahar*)[^10]

pairs.ja: סאלתה ען אלכתאב אלד'י ד'כר פיה ד'לך
pairs.en: I asked him for the book in which this was written
he claimed that he had received it by chain of tradition from his teacher and from his teacher's teacher

fn.10: "Lunar node" (*al-jawzahar*) — the two points at which the moon's orbit intersects the ecliptic, known in Arabic astronomical tradition as the Head and Tail of the Dragon (*raʾs al-tinnīn* and *dhanab al-tinnīn*). The dragon-figure (*dereqon*) of the Mishnah is identified by Rambam's informant with this node. Rambam notes with scholarly skepticism that he could not verify the written source for this claim.

aligned.ja: וכלים מכובדין, הי חלי אלד'הב ואלפצ'ה ות'יאב אלחריר, ומא סוי הד'ה פהי כלים מבוזין. והלכה כרבן שמעון בן גמליאל. וכר' יוסי.
aligned.en: "Honored vessels" (*keilim mekhubadim*) are ornaments of gold and silver and garments of silk; anything other than these is "contemptible vessels" (*keilim mevuzim*). The law follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel. And R. Yosi concurs.[^11]

pairs.en: "Honored vessels" (*keilim mekhubadim*)
ornaments of gold and silver and garments of silk
"contemptible vessels" (*keilim mevuzim*)
The law follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel

fn.11: "R. Yosi concurs" — the text (*ve-khr Yosi*) records R. Yosi's agreement with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's position on "honored" vs. "contemptible" vessels.

aligned.ja: משנה [ד]
aligned.en: Mishnah [4]

aligned.ja: אפרוטידי, אסם כוכב אלזהרה, והכד'א יכתב אסם אלזהרה פי כתב אלטלאסים אפרוטידי וכאן פי הד'א אלחמאם צורהֵ אלזהרה.
aligned.en: *Afroditē* is the name of the planet Venus,[^12] and so the name of Venus is indeed written in the books of talismanic lore as *Afroditē*. There was in this bathhouse a representation of Venus.

pairs.en: *Afroditē* is the name of the planet Venus,[^12]

pairs.ja: יכתב אסם אלזהרה פי כתב אלטלאסים אפרוטידי
pairs.en: the name of Venus is written in the books of talismanic lore as *Afroditē*

pairs.ja: כאן פי הד'א אלחמאם צורהֵ אלזהרה
pairs.en: There was in this bathhouse a representation of Venus

fn.12: *Afroditē* — the Greek name for the goddess Aphrodite, here identified by Rambam with the planet Venus (*Kokhav ha-Nogah*), as the planet bore her name in Greek. Rambam notes that in the books of talismanic lore the name is written in its Greek form *Afroditē* rather than any Hebrew or Arabic equivalent, reflecting the direct transmission of Hellenistic astrological nomenclature in the Jewish and Arabic learned traditions.

aligned.ja: וקולה לה אין משיבין בבית המרחץ, אנמא קאל לה ד'לך בעל כ'רוג'ה מן אלמרחץ פאעתד'ר לה ען סכותה ענד אלסואל וקאל לה אלד'י אוג'ב אן לא נג'אובך לאנה אין משיבין בבית המרחץ.
aligned.en: As for his saying "one does not answer questions in a bathhouse" — Proklos asked R. Gamliel the question upon leaving the bathhouse, and R. Gamliel apologized for his silence during the earlier question by saying to him: what obliged me not to answer you is that one does not give learned discourse in a bathhouse.[^13]

pairs.en: one does not answer questions in a bathhouse

pairs.ja: קאל לה ד'לך בעל כ'רוג'ה מן אלמרחץ
pairs.en: Proklos asked R. Gamliel the question upon leaving the bathhouse

pairs.ja: פאעתד'ר לה ען סכותה ענד אלסואל
pairs.en: R. Gamliel apologized for his silence during the earlier question
what obliged me not to answer you is that one does not give learned discourse in a bathhouse.[^13]

fn.13: The Mishnah records the exchange between the philosopher Proklos and Rabban Gamliel II at the bathhouse of Aphrodite in Acre (BT AZ 44b). R. Gamliel explains that he could not answer inside the bathhouse because such discussions are prohibited there — an explanation that serves, incidentally, to deny that his presence in Aphrodite's bathhouse constituted any acknowledgment of her worship.

aligned.ja: משנה [ה]
aligned.en: Mishnah [5]

aligned.ja: ר' יוסי יעתקד אן אילן שנטעו לשם אילן ולבסוף עבדו אסור לאנה יש בו תפוסת יד אדם. ואלחכמים יקולון אנה מנד' נטעו והו לם יעול פיה עלי אלעבאדה חין גרסה צאר מת'ל הר וגבעה, ועבאדתה בעד ד'לך לא תחרמה.
aligned.en: R. Yosi holds that a tree planted [initially] as an ordinary tree (*ilan*) but subsequently worshipped is forbidden, because it has come under human manipulation (*tafusat yad adam*).[^14] The Sages, however, say that from the moment it was planted it was not treated as an object of worship; it is therefore like a mountain or a hill,[^15] and worship of it thereafter does not render it prohibited.

pairs.ja: אילן שנטעו לשם אילן ולבסוף עבדו אסור
pairs.en: a tree planted as an ordinary tree but subsequently worshipped is forbidden
it has come under human manipulation (*tafusat yad adam*)[^14]
it is therefore like a mountain or a hill[^15]
worship of it thereafter does not render it prohibited

fn.14: "Human manipulation" (*tafusat yad adam*) — lit. "the grasp of a human hand," the legal criterion R. Yosi uses to distinguish objects that can bear forbidden status: a mountain or rock cannot be forbidden since it was not shaped by human hands, but a planted tree, though natural, was established by human agency and therefore can acquire forbidden status.
fn.15: "Like a mountain or a hill" — the Mishnah's principle that natural objects (*har ve-givʿah*) cannot become forbidden because no human act created them. The Sages extend this logic to a tree planted for ordinary agricultural purposes.

aligned.ja: ור' עקיבה אעלמנא באצל נבחת' בה ען מואצ'ע עבודה זרה ולם יכ'אלף אחד. ואין הלכה כר' יוסי.
aligned.en: R. Akiva has taught us a ruling that serves as a basis for investigating sites of idolatry, and no one disputes it. The law does not follow R. Yosi.

pairs.en: R. Akiva has taught us a ruling

pairs.ja: נבחת' בה ען מואצ'ע עבודה זרה
pairs.en: for investigating sites of idolatry
no one disputes it
The law does not follow R. Yosi

aligned.ja: משנה [ו]
aligned.en: Mishnah [6]

aligned.ja: מע כונה כונס לתוך שלו, לכנה לא יתרך ד'לך אלפצ'א לעבודה זרה לאנה ינפעהא, בל יעמרהא באמור קד'רה או ימלאה שוך ונחוה.
aligned.en: "Even though it encroaches upon his own domain" — nonetheless he may not leave that space to the idol, since that would benefit it; rather, he should fill it with stones or thorns and the like.

pairs.en: it encroaches upon his own domain

pairs.ja: לא יתרך ד'לך אלפצ'א לעבודה זרה
pairs.en: he may not leave that space to the idol
since that would benefit it
fill it with stones or thorns and the like

aligned.ja: ואעלם אן טומאת עבודה זרה דרבנן, פלד'לך יאכ'ד'ון פיהא באלתכ'פיף מן כל וג'ה, פיקולון אנהא שבהת באלשרץ לתנג'ס במגע לא במשא כשרץ, ושבהת באלנדה לאנהא אינה מטמאה אברים כאלנדה אלתי לא ינג'ס ידהא או רג'להא אן קטעת משום נדה, ושבהת באלמת אנהא לא תטמא אלא כזית לא אקל מן ד'לך.
aligned.en: Know that the ritual impurity of an idol is Rabbinic in origin (*de-rabbanan*),[^16] and for this reason the Sages treated it leniently in every respect. They compared it to the creeping thing (*sheretz*),[^17] in that it conveys impurity by contact but not by carrying, as the sheretz does; they compared it to the menstruant (*niddah*),[^18] in that it does not impart impurity to limbs — just as a niddah's severed hand or foot does not impart impurity by reason of being niddah; and they compared it to the corpse (*met*),[^19] in that it conveys impurity only when there is an olive's bulk (*ke-zayit*) and not less.

pairs.en: the ritual impurity of an idol is Rabbinic in origin (*de-rabbanan*)[^16]

pairs.ja: שבהת באלשרץ לתנג'ס במגע לא במשא
pairs.en: compared it to the creeping thing (*sheretz*),[^17] in that it conveys impurity by contact but not by carrying

pairs.ja: שבהת באלנדה לאנהא אינה מטמאה אברים
pairs.en: compared it to the menstruant (*niddah*),[^18] in that it does not impart impurity to limbs

pairs.ja: שבהת באלמת אנהא לא תטמא אלא כזית
pairs.en: compared it to the corpse (*met*),[^19] in that it conveys impurity only when there is an olive's bulk (*ke-zayit*)

fn.16: "Rabbinic in origin" (*de-rabbanan*) — the ritual impurity assigned to an idol is a Rabbinic enactment rather than a Biblical one, which is why the Sages can treat it with various leniencies. Rambam's explicit statement here is philosophically significant: he grounds the entire subsequent legal discussion in the secondary status of this impurity.
fn.17: *Sheretz* — one of the eight categories of creeping things listed in Lev 11:29–30, whose carcasses convey impurity only through contact, not through carrying (*massa*).
fn.18: *Niddah* — the menstruant, whose ritual impurity is treated as highly contagious in most contexts, but whose severed limb does not convey niddah-impurity to others, since her impurity is bodily-constitutional rather than inherent in each limb separately.
fn.19: *Met* (corpse) — human corpse-impurity is the most severe category in Biblical law, but even a corpse conveys impurity only through pieces of at least an olive's bulk (*ke-zayit*), not through smaller fragments.

aligned.ja: ואין הלכה כר' עקיבה ולו פי עבודה זרה נפסהא פכיף משמשיה.
aligned.en: The law does not follow R. Akiva even with respect to an idol itself, and certainly not with respect to its accessories (*meshamsheha*).

pairs.en: The law does not follow R. Akiva
even with respect to an idol itself
certainly not with respect to its accessories (*meshamsheha*)

aligned.ja: משנה [ז]
aligned.en: Mishnah [7]

aligned.ja: סיוד, אלתביץ' באלגיר. וכיור, אלנקש ואלתצויר. וקולה וחדש, תקדירה או שחדשו. וחלפין, תתסמי אלאגצאן אלתי נבתת בדל אלתי קטעת והו קולה והחליף.
aligned.en: *Siud* means whitewashing with lime. *Kiyur* means plastering and painting.[^20] His saying "and [that which is] renewed" (*ve-ḥadash*) is to be read as if it said "or that which they renewed" (*o she-ḥiddeshu*). *Ḥalifin* is the name given to branches that have sprouted in place of those that were cut — this is the meaning of "and its new growth" (*ve-ha-ḥalif*).

pairs.en: *Siud* means whitewashing with lime
*Kiyur* means plastering and painting.[^20]

pairs.ja: חלפין, תתסמי אלאגצאן אלתי נבתת בדל אלתי קטעת
pairs.en: *Ḥalifin* is the name given to branches that have sprouted in place of those that were cut

fn.20: The Mishnah discusses renovating an asherah tree: *siud* (whitewashing) and *kiyur* (decorative carving or painting) enhance the tree's sanctity for idol-worshippers and thereby deepen its forbidden status.

aligned.ja: וקולה אי זו היא אשרה, אנמא יריד בה אי זו היא אשרה שנחלקו בה חכמים ור' שמעון, לאנה קד קאל אן אלאשרות ת'לאת'ה אנואע, את'נתין לא אכ'תלאף פי חכמהא, ואלת'אלת'ה והי אלתי תכון תחתהא עבודה זרה יקול אלחכמים אנהא אסורה בהנאה טאל מא עבודה זרה תחתהא, פאד'א אזאלהא מן תחתהא חיניד' תחל כמא תקדם מן קולהם העמיד תחתיו עבודה זרה ובטלה הרי זה מותר.
aligned.en: His question "which asherah[^21] is this?" refers to which asherah it is that the Sages and R. Shimon disagree about, for he has stated that asherot fall into three types: two types are uncontested in their ruling, while the third — one beneath which an idol stands — is the one regarding which the Sages say it is forbidden to derive benefit (*asur be-hana'ah*)[^22] for as long as the idol stands beneath it; once the idol is removed from beneath it, the tree becomes permitted, in line with their earlier position that "if he placed an idol beneath it and then nullified it, it is permitted."

pairs.ja: אי זו היא אשרה שנחלקו בה חכמים ור' שמעון
pairs.en: which asherah[^21] it is that the Sages and R. Shimon disagree about
asherot fall into three types
forbidden to derive benefit (*asur be-hana'ah*)[^22]
for as long as the idol stands beneath it

pairs.ja: פאד'א אזאלהא מן תחתהא חיניד' תחל
pairs.en: once the idol is removed from beneath it, the tree becomes permitted

fn.21: *Asherah* — a sacred tree (or grove) worshipped in Canaanite religion, prohibited by the Torah (Deut 16:21). The Mishnah distinguishes several legal categories depending on whether the tree was planted from the outset for worship, planted ordinarily but later worshipped, or used merely as a canopy for a separate idol.
fn.22: "Forbidden to derive benefit" (*asur be-hana'ah*) — the prohibition on all benefit (*hana'ah*) from an object, not merely on eating it or using it ritually. An asherah used as a canopy for an idol is forbidden to derive any benefit from as long as it serves that function.

aligned.ja: ור' שמעון יקול אפילו לא בטלה ואף על פי שהיא תחתיו הואיל ולצורה עובדין מותר. ואין הלכה כר' שמעון.
aligned.en: R. Shimon says: even if the idol has not been nullified and still stands beneath the tree, since worship is directed at the figure [of the idol] and not at the tree, the tree is permitted. The law does not follow R. Shimon.

pairs.ja: ר' שמעון יקול אפילו לא בטלה
pairs.en: R. Shimon says: even if the idol has not been nullified
since worship is directed at the figure the tree is permitted
The law does not follow R. Shimon

aligned.ja: משנה [ח]
aligned.en: Mishnah [8]

aligned.ja: לא ישב בצלה, פי ט'ל ד'את אלשג'רה, אמא ט'ל אגצאנהא וורקהא פיג'וז לה אלג'לוס הנאך. והד'א אלד'י קלנא אם עבר טמא, לאנא נקול לא בד הנאך מן תקרובת עבודה זרה.
aligned.en: "He may not sit in its shade" — this refers to the shade cast by the trunk of the tree. But sitting in the shade of its branches and leaves is permitted. The statement that "if he transgressed and sat, he is impure" means: we hold that under such a tree there must inevitably be offerings of idolatry (*taqrovet avodah zarah*).[^23]

pairs.ja: לא ישב בצלה, פי ט'ל ד'את אלשג'רה
pairs.en: "He may not sit in its shade" — this refers to the shade cast by the trunk of the tree

pairs.ja: ט'ל אגצאנהא וורקהא פיג'וז לה אלג'לוס
pairs.en: sitting in the shade of its branches and leaves is permitted

pairs.ja: לא בד הנאך מן תקרובת עבודה זרה
pairs.en: under such a tree there must inevitably be offerings of idolatry (*taqrovet avodah zarah*)[^23]

fn.23: "Offerings of idolatry" (*taqrovet avodah zarah*) — food or other items offered to an idol in the course of worship. Rambam explains that R. Yehudah ben Beteirah infers that such offerings conveyed impurity by overhanging (*ohel*), as a corpse does, from the verse that equates the sacrifices of Baal Peor with "sacrifices of the dead" (Num 25:5).

aligned.ja: והד'א מד'הב ר' יהודה בן בתירה אלד'י יקול מנין לתקרובת עבודה זרה שהיא מטמא באהל שנ' ויצמדו לבעל פעור ויאכלו זבחי מתים, מה מת מטמא באהל אף תקרובת עבודה זרה מטמא באהל.
aligned.en: This is the position of R. Yehudah ben Beteirah, who says: whence do we learn that offerings of idolatry convey impurity by means of an overhanging roof (*ohel*)? As it is written, "they were joined to Baal Peor and ate the sacrifices of the dead" (Num 25:5) — just as a corpse conveys impurity by means of an overhanging roof, so too do offerings of idolatry.[^24]

pairs.en: the position of R. Yehudah ben Beteirah

pairs.ja: מנין לתקרובת עבודה זרה שהיא מטמא באהל
pairs.en: whence do we learn that offerings of idolatry convey impurity by means of an overhanging roof (*ohel*)

pairs.ja: ויצמדו לבעל פעור ויאכלו זבחי מתים
pairs.en: "they were joined to Baal Peor and ate the sacrifices of the dead"

pairs.ja: מה מת מטמא באהל אף תקרובת עבודה זרה מטמא באהל
pairs.en: just as a corpse conveys impurity by means of an overhanging roof, so too do offerings of idolatry.[^24]

fn.24: The analogy of *ohel* (tent/overhanging) impurity: Biblical law holds that a corpse conveys impurity to any person or vessel under the same roof (Num 19:14). R. Yehudah ben Beteirah derives by analogy that idol-offerings, compared to "sacrifices of the dead," do the same.

aligned.ja: ואין הלכה כר' יהודה בן בתירה, לאנהא מא שבהת עבודה זרה באלמית אלא לאנהא לא תנג'ס באקל מן כזית כמת עלי מא בינא, ואנמא תנג'ס תקרובת עבודה זרה במגע ובמשא כנבלה.
aligned.en: The law does not follow R. Yehudah ben Beteirah, for the idol was compared to a corpse only in that it does not convey impurity with less than an olive's bulk, as we explained; offerings of idolatry convey impurity only by contact and by carrying, as an animal carcass (*nevelah*) does.[^25]

pairs.ja: ואין הלכה כר' יהודה בן בתירה
pairs.en: The law does not follow R. Yehudah ben Beteirah

pairs.ja: לא תנג'ס באקל מן כזית כמת
pairs.en: it does not convey impurity with less than an olive's bulk

pairs.ja: תנג'ס תקרובת עבודה זרה במגע ובמשא
pairs.en: offerings of idolatry convey impurity only by contact and by carrying
as an animal carcass (*nevelah*) does.[^25]

fn.25: *Nevelah* — the carcass of an animal that died without proper ritual slaughter, which conveys impurity through contact and carrying (*maga* and *massa*) but not through overhanging (*ohel*). Rambam rules that idol-offerings follow this lower level of impurity, not the corpse-level impurity R. Yehudah ben Beteirah proposes.

aligned.ja: וגוזלת את הרבים, אן תכון אגצאנהא ממתדה עלי הוא רשות הרבים. ואלכ'ס והו החזרין יאד'יה כת'רהֵ אלמא אלנאזל מן אלסמא, פלד'לך לא יזרע תחתהא ולו פי אלשתא לאנהא תנפעה.
aligned.en: "It encroaches upon public space" (*gozelet et ha-rabbim*) means that its branches extend over the public thoroughfare. The *khas* — that is, the carob tree (*al-kharūb*) — is harmed by the abundance of rainwater that falls from it, and therefore one may not sow beneath it even in winter, since the tree benefits [from what is sown].[^26]

pairs.en: "It encroaches upon public space" (*gozelet et ha-rabbim*)

pairs.ja: אגצאנהא ממתדה עלי הוא רשות הרבים
pairs.en: its branches extend over the public thoroughfare

pairs.ja: אלכ'ס והו החזרין יאד'יה כת'רהֵ אלמא
pairs.en: The *khas* — that is, the carob tree (*al-kharūb*) — is harmed by the abundance of rainwater

pairs.ja: לא יזרע תחתהא ולו פי אלשתא לאנהא תנפעה
pairs.en: one may not sow beneath it even in winter, since the tree benefits [from what is sown].[^26]

fn.26: The carob tree (*ḥarūv* / *khas*) sheds large quantities of water that fall from its canopy during rain; that runoff benefits plants grown beneath it. Since the tree is an asherah, any agricultural benefit it provides would be forbidden — hence one may not sow beneath it even in the rainy season when the benefit is indirect.

aligned.ja: וקד תקדם לך מד'הב ר' יוסי פי הד'א אלפרק אנה לא יראעי רג'וע עבודה זרה ומשמשיה זבל, לאן ליס ד'לך אלזבל וחדה הו סבב אלנבאת, בל אלזבל ואלארץ' ואלמא ואלהוא ואלשמס, והו יעתקד זה וזה גורם מותר, אעני אן ינפעל שי מא יכון אסבאב אנפעאלה מנהא חראם ומנהא חלאל פד'לך אלשי אלמנפעל חלאל.
aligned.en: We have already set forth R. Yosi's position in this chapter: he does not reckon the return of idolatry's accessories as manure, for manure alone is not the sole cause of plant growth — growth is caused by manure, soil, water, air, and sun together — and his ruling is that "when both this and that are causative, it is permitted" (*zeh ve-zeh gorem mutar*),[^27] meaning that if the causes of a thing's action include some that are forbidden and some that are permitted, the resultant thing is permitted.

pairs.ja: לא יראעי רג'וע עבודה זרה ומשמשיה זבל
pairs.en: he does not reckon the return of idolatry's accessories as manure

pairs.ja: ליס ד'לך אלזבל וחדה הו סבב אלנבאת
pairs.en: manure alone is not the sole cause of plant growth
"when both this and that are causative, it is permitted" (*zeh ve-zeh gorem mutar*)[^27]

pairs.ja: אסבאב אנפעאלה מנהא חראם ומנהא חלאל
pairs.en: the causes of a thing's action include some that are forbidden and some that are permitted

fn.27: *Zeh ve-zeh gorem mutar* — "when both this and that are causative, it is permitted" — R. Yosi's principle that when a forbidden cause and a permitted cause jointly produce an outcome, the outcome is permitted, since neither cause alone was sufficient. This ruling is the operative halakhah.

aligned.ja: וכד'לך קטוע אלהלכה פי ג'מיע אלאשיא, ואנמא קאל הנא הד'א אלכלאם כאלמעתרץ' לאלחכמים, לאנה קאל להם עלי מד'הבכם אלד'ין תראעון רג'וע עבודה זרה זבל אף לא ירקות בימות הגשמים. וקד בינא אן אלהלכה כר' יוסי ועלי מד'הבה אלעמל.
aligned.en: This is the definitive ruling in all such matters. He introduced this argument here as a counterpoint to the Sages, saying to them: according to your own position, in which you reckon the return of idolatrous articles as manure — then surely one may not [sow] vegetables even in the rainy season. We have established that the law follows R. Yosi, and practice is in accordance with his view.

pairs.en: the definitive ruling in all such matters

pairs.ja: קאל הנא הד'א אלכלאם כאלמעתרץ' לאלחכמים
pairs.en: He introduced this argument here as a counterpoint to the Sages
surely one may not [sow] vegetables even in the rainy season

pairs.ja: אלהלכה כר' יוסי ועלי מד'הבה אלעמל
pairs.en: the law follows R. Yosi, and practice is in accordance with his view

aligned.ja: משנה [ט]
aligned.en: Mishnah [9]

aligned.ja: אול חמיה יחמי אלתנור בהא תם טבך' שקפה ויצלח ליטבך' פיה פי מא בעד, פלד'לך יותץ, לאנה ואן ברד פאידהֵ תלך אלתסכ'ינה באקיה פיה. והד'א עלי מד'הב מן יקול זה וזה גורם אסור.
aligned.en: The initial firing heats the oven and burns into it a residue so that even after it cools one can cook in it going forward; it must therefore be demolished (*yutatz*), for even after it has cooled the benefit of that initial heating persists within it. This ruling accords with the position of the one who holds that "when both this and that are causative, it is forbidden."[^28]

pairs.en: The initial firing heats the oven
it must therefore be demolished (*yutatz*)
the benefit of that initial heating persists within it
"when both this and that are causative, it is forbidden."[^28]

fn.28: The opposite principle, *zeh ve-zeh gorem asur* — "when both causative, it is forbidden" — holds that any contribution of a forbidden cause to a final product renders that product forbidden. Rambam notes that the ruling about the oven follows this stricter position, but then states that the definitive halakhah requires only re-firing the oven with permitted fuel, implying the lenient principle ultimately governs.

aligned.ja: וקטוע אלהלכה בין חדש בין ישן יוצן, אעני אנה יתרך חתי יברד ויחמי ת'אניה בעצים של התר ויטבך' פיה וד'לך חלאל.
aligned.en: The definitive ruling, however, between [oven] new and old alike, is that it be left to cool and then re-fired a second time with permitted wood, after which cooking in it is permitted.

pairs.ja: קטוע אלהלכה בין חדש בין ישן
pairs.en: The definitive ruling, between oven new and old alike
it be left to cool
re-fired a second time with permitted wood
cooking in it is permitted

aligned.ja: וקול ר' אליעזר יוליך הנייה לים המלח, הו אן יאכ'ד' מן ת'מנהא ת'מן ד'לך אלרגיף אלמכ'תלט פי ג'מלהֵ אלכ'בז וירמיה פי אלבחר אלמאלח חית' לא יוצל אליה אבדא.
aligned.en: R. Eliezer's ruling that "he should take the monetary value of the benefit and cast it into the Dead Sea" means: he should take from the price of that loaf of bread — the loaf baked in the forbidden fire that became mixed in with the rest of the bread — an amount equal to the value of that loaf, and throw it into the sea where it can never be retrieved.

pairs.en: he should take the monetary value of the benefit and cast it into the Dead Sea

pairs.ja: יאכ'ד' מן ת'מנהא ת'מן ד'לך אלרגיף
pairs.en: he should take from the price the value of that loaf of bread
throw it into the sea
where it can never be retrieved

aligned.ja: וד'כר אכ'תלאפהם פי אלפת ואלבגד, אן ולו פי אלבגד אלתי אלכ'לאל אלתי נסג' בה אלת'וב באקיא ואיתיה לאסורא בעיניה יקול רבי אליעזר יוליך הנייה לים המלח, ולו פי אלפת אלד'י תלף אלחטב וליתיה לאסורא יקולון אלחכמים כולן אסורות.
aligned.en: He then discusses their disagreement concerning the bread (*pat*) and the garment (*beged*): regarding the garment, where the warp threads that were woven into it remain as such and are themselves forbidden, R. Eliezer says he should cast the monetary value of the benefit into the Dead Sea; but regarding the bread, where the wood is entirely consumed and only its thermal effect lingers, all the Sages say the entire baked product is forbidden.

pairs.en: their disagreement concerning the bread (*pat*) and the garment (*beged*)

pairs.ja: אלבגד אלתי אלכ'לאל אלתי נסג' בה אלת'וב באקיא
pairs.en: the garment, where the warp threads that were woven into it remain
the bread, where the wood is entirely consumed
all the Sages say the entire baked product is forbidden

aligned.ja: והלכה כר' אליעזר פי אלכל, ולו חבית של יין נסך אד'א אכ'תלטת בין החביות יוליך הנייה לים המלח ויג'וז לה ביע אלג'מיע ואלאסתנפאע בה.
aligned.en: The law follows R. Eliezer in all cases — and even a barrel of libation wine (*yayin nesekh*)[^29] that became mixed among other barrels: one should cast the monetary value of the benefit into the Dead Sea, and it is then permitted to sell the entire lot and to derive benefit from it.

pairs.en: The law follows R. Eliezer in all cases

pairs.ja: חבית של יין נסך אד'א אכ'תלטת בין החביות
pairs.en: a barrel of libation wine (*yayin nesekh*)[^29] that became mixed among other barrels
cast the monetary value of the benefit into the Dead Sea

pairs.ja: ויג'וז לה ביע אלג'מיע ואלאסתנפאע בה
pairs.en: it is then permitted to sell the entire lot and to derive benefit from it

fn.29: *Yayin nesekh* — wine used for libation to an idol, forbidden Biblically (as distinct from *stam yeinam*, ordinary wine of idolaters, which is only Rabbinically forbidden). Even when a barrel of *yayin nesekh* becomes mixed with other barrels, R. Eliezer's rule of casting the monetary benefit into the sea resolves the situation and permits sale of the mixture.

aligned.ja: משנה [י]
aligned.en: Mishnah [10]

aligned.ja: קרסום, קטע אלאטראף. וזירוד, קטע אלאגצאן. שפיה, ג'רדהא. והד'א כלה באן יפעלה גוי, לאן אלאצל ענדנא אנה לא יבטל עבודה זרה אלא גוי שיודע בטיב עבודה זרה ומשמשיה, והכד'א קאלוא דפלח מבטל דלא פלח לא מבטל.
aligned.en: *Qirseum* means trimming the extremities; *zirud* means cutting the branches; *shepiya* means scraping it bare. All of this is done by an idolater — for our principle is that an idol can be nullified (*bittul*)[^30] only by an idolater who knows the ways of idol worship and its accessories. This is what is meant by the saying: "one who worships it can nullify it; one who does not worship it cannot nullify it."

pairs.en: *Qirseum* means trimming the extremities
*zirud* means cutting the branches

pairs.ja: לא יבטל עבודה זרה אלא גוי שיודע בטיב עבודה זרה
pairs.en: an idol can be nullified (*bittul*)[^30] only by an idolater who knows the ways of idol worship

pairs.ja: דפלח מבטל דלא פלח לא מבטל
pairs.en: "one who worships it can nullify it; one who does not worship it cannot nullify it"

fn.30: *Bittul* (nullification) — the legal act by which an idol's forbidden status is annulled. Rambam establishes that only an idolater who genuinely practices idol-worship can perform *bittul*, since only someone who treats the idol as a deity can meaningfully renounce or degrade it. A child or intellectually impaired person whose worship is not halakhically cognizant cannot effect nullification.

aligned.ja: ומעני קולי בטיב עבודה זרה אן לא יכון צבי צגיר או מכ'תל אלתמייז.
aligned.en: The meaning of my phrase "knows the ways of idol worship" is that the idolater not be a young child or one whose discernment is impaired.

pairs.en: The meaning of my phrase "knows the ways of idol worship"
that the idolater not be a young child
or one whose discernment is impaired
